what: On wide screens (782px or more · aspect ratio 3:1 or less) the sections line up in a single row, each one screen tall, and vertical wheel · trackpad scrolling is received by Lenis as horizontal scroll (duration 1 · default curve 1.001−2^(−10t)), turning the page into a scroll that glides sideways. When the screen becomes narrow or very wide, Lenis is removed and the sections go back to a normal vertically stacked page

options.min: Minimum width (px) at which the horizontal scroll turns on, default 782
options.aspect: Max aspect ratio at which it turns on, default 3/1 — anything wider makes the sheet too short, so it stays vertical
options.dur: Length of one roll slide (seconds), default 1
options.fx:side: Event emitted when the element turns on and off (detail.side) — for when the consumer re-measures a motion that reads the horizontal scroll position (scrollX)
options.el.lenis: Lenis attached to the element while on — used like lenis.stop() when opening the menu

note: It uses window scroll, so only one is attached per page (a second one steps aside). Section width is set by the consumer (100vw, fixed px or content width). With reduced motion on, it moves sideways right away by the amount scrolled with no smoothing (lerp 1). Converting vertical scroll into horizontal movement still works as usual

from.where: index.html .dk-main (original body.lenis-horizontal — new Lenis({ autoRaf: true, orientation: "horizontal", duration: 1 }), (min-width:782px) and (max-aspect-ratio:3/1) only. The site-wide version does the same thing with shared.js lenisInit)
